title: Events platform example

CTX.name: Accounts & organisers
CTX.desc: People who sign in, organisations that host events, and their team memberships.

CTX.name: Events
CTX.desc: Reusable event listings, their dated occurrences, and discovery categories.

CTX.name: Venues
CTX.desc: Physical venues and their bookable rooms or spaces.

CTX.name: Programme
CTX.desc: The sessions and speakers within an event occurrence.

CTX.name: Ticketing
CTX.desc: Ticket products, capacity, sales windows, and temporary checkout reservations.

CTX.name: Sales & payments
CTX.desc: Purchases, price snapshots, discounts, payment attempts, and partial refunds.

CTX.name: Attendance
CTX.desc: Ticket holders, issued tickets, transfers, admission records, and waiting lists.

CTX.name: Communications
CTX.desc: Event announcements and a record of each email delivery.

ENT.desc: A sign-in account. A buyer, organiser team member, or attendee may use the same account. Authentication secrets belong in a separate identity system.

f.note: Unique after trimming and case-insensitive comparison.

ENT.desc: An organisation or individual that owns event listings and receives their sales proceeds.
checks: At least one active OrganizerMember has the owner role.

ENT.desc: Connects an account to an organiser team and records its role. One account can belong to several organisers.
A reusable discovery category, such as music or workshops. This is a controlled classification, not an event owner.
The public listing and shared description of an event. Each dated run is an EventOccurrence; recurring events reuse this listing.
An explicit link that allows an event to appear in multiple categories without duplicating event or category data.
One dated run of an event. It has its own time, location, capacity, programme, ticket products, and waiting list.

f.note: IANA time-zone name used to display the UTC timestamps.
Maximum number of issued valid tickets plus active, unexpired reserved places.

checks: ends_at > starts_at; capacity >= 0.
At least one of venue_space_id and online_url is present; both may be set for a hybrid event.
For a physical occurrence, capacity <= its venue space capacity.

ENT.desc: A physical location that can contain one or more event spaces. The address is a value object, not a separate business entity.
A room, hall, stage, or other bookable space within a venue. Different event occurrences can reuse the same space.
checks: capacity > 0.

ENT.desc: A talk, performance, workshop, or other scheduled activity within one occurrence. Sessions do not sell separate tickets in this example.
checks: starts_at < ends_at; the session is within its occurrence time range.
When venue_space_id is set, it belongs to the occurrence venue.

ENT.desc: A reusable public speaker or performer profile. Being a speaker does not require having a sign-in account.
Connects speakers to sessions. A session can have several speakers, and a speaker can appear in several sessions.

f.note: For example host, speaker, or performer.

checks: display_order >= 0.

ENT.desc: A sellable ticket product for one occurrence, such as general admission or a concession. Capacity and sales windows belong to this product.
checks: capacity >= 0; max_per_order > 0.
sales_start_at < sales_end_at <= occurrence.starts_at.
Issued non-voided tickets plus active, unexpired reservations do not exceed ticket-type capacity or occurrence capacity.

ENT.desc: A temporary hold on a ticket quantity during checkout. Conversion releases the hold as the matching tickets are issued; an expired hold does not consume capacity.
checks: quantity > 0 and quantity <= ticket_type.max_per_order.
An active reservation counts only while expires_at is in the future.
A converted reservation matches the quantity of its order item and is replaced by issued tickets.

ENT.desc: An organiser-owned discount, optionally restricted to one event. Its terms are copied into order-item price snapshots at purchase time.

f.note: Three-letter currency code; required for a fixed-amount discount.

checks: valid_from < valid_until; value > 0; max_redemptions is absent or > 0.
Percentage discounts have value <= 100 and no currency; fixed-amount discounts require a currency.
A restricted event belongs to the same organiser; a code applies only to eligible orders.

ENT.desc: One checkout with a single organiser and currency. The buyer may purchase tickets for several attendees; guest checkout does not require an account.

f.note: Contact snapshot retained with the purchase.

checks: All order items belong to this organiser and use the order currency.
total.amount equals the sum of order-item totals.
A confirmed order has at least one item; successful payments cover its total. Free orders need no payment.
A discount is redeemed once per confirmed order; confirmed redemptions do not exceed its limit.

ENT.desc: A purchased quantity of one ticket type. Price, discount, and tax are immutable snapshots; later ticket-price changes do not change this purchase.
checks: quantity > 0 and quantity <= ticket_type.max_per_order.
All money values use the order currency; discount <= quantity * unit_price.
total.amount = quantity * unit_price.amount - discount.amount + tax.amount.
A confirmed order item issues exactly quantity tickets; voided tickets remain in its history.

ENT.desc: One payment attempt against an order. Failed attempts are retained and a later attempt has a separate identity. No card numbers or payment secrets are stored.
checks: amount.amount > 0 and uses the order currency.
The sum of successful payments does not exceed the order total; paid_at is present for succeeded payments.

ENT.desc: One full or partial return of a successful payment. The affected order-item quantities are recorded in RefundItem.
checks: The payment succeeded; the refund uses its currency and has a positive amount.
amount.amount equals the sum of refund-item amounts.
Succeeded plus pending refunds do not exceed the payment amount; succeeded refunds have refunded_at.

ENT.desc: Allocates a refund to a quantity from one original order item, making partial ticket refunds explicit.
checks: quantity > 0; amount.amount > 0; the order item belongs to the refunded payment order.
Pending and succeeded refunded quantities and amounts do not exceed the original order item.
A succeeded refund voids exactly quantity tickets linked to this refund item.

ENT.desc: A person who can hold tickets or join a waiting list. The attendee may differ from the buyer and may optionally link to a sign-in account.
One issued admission for one person, derived from its order item and ticket type. It may be unassigned until claimed; the buyer is not automatically the attendee.

f.note: Opaque, unique admission identifier; no personal data is embedded.

checks: The order is confirmed; its order item identifies the occurrence and ticket type.
checked_in requires a CheckIn; voided tickets cannot be admitted or transferred.
A refund_item_id points to a succeeded refund for the same order item and requires status voided.

ENT.desc: An invitation to hand an unused ticket to someone else. Email and sender identity are retained even before the recipient claims the ticket.
checks: At most one pending transfer per ticket; the ticket is valid and has no CheckIn.
An accepted transfer has to_attendee_id and accepted_at, and assigns the ticket to that attendee.

ENT.desc: The admission record for one ticket. A unique ticket reference prevents a second admission; optional gate information records where it happened.
checks: The ticket is assigned to an attendee and is not voided.
The staff account belongs to the occurrence organiser team.

ENT.desc: A request for places at a sold-out occurrence, optionally for a specific ticket type. Offers can link to a temporary reservation during checkout.
uk: (occurrence_id, attendee_id) while status is waiting or offered
checks: quantity > 0; a selected ticket type belongs to the same occurrence.
An offered entry has offered_at < offer_expires_at; any linked reservation matches the occurrence and quantity.
A converted entry points to a converted reservation.

ENT.desc: An organiser message for an event, such as a programme update. Drafts become published announcements, with a separate delivery record for each recipient.
checks: A published announcement has published_at.

ENT.desc: One email delivery of a published announcement to an attendee. The destination address is a snapshot, and failures remain visible for retry.
checks: The announcement is published; attempt_count >= 0; sent deliveries have sent_at.

ENUMNOTES.AccountStatus: Whether an account can use the service.
ENUMNOTES.OrganizerRole: Access role within one organiser team.
ENUMNOTES.EventStatus: Publication state of the shared event listing.
ENUMNOTES.OccurrenceStatus: State of one dated run, independently of other runs.
ENUMNOTES.ReservationStatus: Whether a checkout hold still consumes ticket capacity.
ENUMNOTES.DiscountKind: Interpretation of the discount value and optional currency.
ENUMNOTES.OrderStatus: State of one checkout; confirmed orders retain their financial history.
ENUMNOTES.TicketStatus: Admission validity of one issued ticket.
ENUMNOTES.TransferStatus: Progress of an invitation to reassign a ticket.
ENUMNOTES.WaitlistStatus: Progress from waiting for availability through an offer to purchase.
ENUMNOTES.AnnouncementStatus: Whether an event message is ready for recipients.
ENUMNOTES.DeliveryStatus: Outcome of sending one announcement email.

f.note: Three-letter currency code, for example EUR or USD.

TYPES.d: An exact amount paired with a three-letter currency code. Amounts are nonnegative and use the currency fractional precision; values in different currencies cannot be added.
A physical address stored as one value object on a venue.

PRIMS: An absolute timestamp stored in UTC.
